The flags of the United States and State of Florida will be lowered from sunrise to sunset on Saturday, September 26, at the State Capitol in…
item.content:encoded:
Governor Ron DeSantis has directed flags to be flown at half-staff Saturday in honor of former Flagler Beach Mayor Alice M. Baker, according to a memorandum issued Friday by the Governor's Press Office.

The flags of the United States and State of Florida will be lowered from sunrise to sunset on Saturday, September 26, at the State Capitol in Tallahassee and at all local and state buildings, installations, and grounds throughout Flagler Beach.

The directive was issued to Brian Fienemann, Director of Real Estate Management and Development, and current Flagler Beach Mayor Patti King. No additional details about Baker's death or tenure were provided in the announcement.

item.title: Santa Rosa County Libraries Mark 20 Years With Anniversary Celebration Oct. 3
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Santa Rosa County's library system is throwing open its doors Saturday, October 3rd, for a special 20th anniversary celebration across all system locations. The event runs from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. and will feature activities for all ages, giving the community a chance to mark two decades of library services in the county. According to Santa Rosa…
item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County's library system is throwing open its doors Saturday, October 3rd, for a special 20th anniversary celebration across all system locations. The event runs from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. and will feature activities for all ages, giving the community a chance to mark two decades of library services in the county.

According to Santa Rosa County Communications, all regular library locations will participate in the milestone celebration. The Milton Library, which is temporarily closed, has directed patrons to join the festivities at one of the other branch locations instead.

Beyond the anniversary event, Santa Rosa County Libraries is rolling out its full fall schedule, which includes returning preschool storytime programs at multiple branches—Gulf Breeze, Jay, Navarre, and Pace libraries—running through early December. Toddler Time programs for children 18 to 36 months are also back, though those require advance registration and have limited space.

The system is also hosting a bilingual traveling exhibit called "Indios Amigos" starting October 5th at Gulf Breeze Library, highlighting the Aztec artisans and warriors who came with Tristan de Luna's 1559 expedition to Pensacola. For genealogy enthusiasts, family history assistance will be available at select branches throughout October. More details on all programs and events are available at www.santarosa.fl.gov/libraries.

item.title: Senator Moody backs bill to shield Florida ratepayers from data center costs
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Senator Ashley Moody is co-sponsoring federal legislation aimed at preventing everyday Floridians from bearing the cost of massive data center construction and operation. The Ratepayer Protection Act, introduced by Ohio Senator John Husted, passed the House of Representatives by an overwhelming 417-3 margin but has stalled in the Senate after…
item.content:encoded:
Senator Ashley Moody is co-sponsoring federal legislation aimed at preventing everyday Floridians from bearing the cost of massive data center construction and operation. The Ratepayer Protection Act, introduced by Ohio Senator John Husted, passed the House of Representatives by an overwhelming 417-3 margin but has stalled in the Senate after Democrats blocked its advancement, according to a press release issued today.

The bill would require state utility regulators and unregulated utilities to ensure that large data center operators pay the full cost of any power grid upgrades needed to serve their facilities—including generation, transmission, and distribution improvements. It would also mandate that data centers provide financial guarantees before utilities make those upgrades and cover costs if they exit their power contracts early.

"I'm cosponsoring the Ratepayer Protection Act to ensure Americans are protected from increased costs associated with new data centers," Moody said in a statement. "If billion-dollar tech companies want to build a massive data center, Floridians should not be left to foot the bill."

Moody has previously staked out a firm position on data centers, consistently backing local community control over where such facilities are sited. As artificial intelligence and cloud computing drive demand for data centers nationwide, the question of who pays for infrastructure upgrades has become increasingly contentious, particularly in states like Florida where growth pressures are mounting.

item.title: FDOT warns of major I-10, I-110 closures next week in Escambia County
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Drivers throughout Escambia and Santa Rosa counties should prepare for significant traffic disruptions over the next week as the Florida Department of Transportation stages multiple construction and resurfacing projects on major corridors. The most impactful work will hit Interstate 10 and Interstate 110, where crews will close lanes nightly from…
item.content:encoded:
Drivers throughout Escambia and Santa Rosa counties should prepare for significant traffic disruptions over the next week as the Florida Department of Transportation stages multiple construction and resurfacing projects on major corridors.

The most impactful work will hit Interstate 10 and Interstate 110, where crews will close lanes nightly from Sunday, September 27 through Thursday, October 1, between 8 p.m. and 6 a.m. On I-10, expect intermittent closures between mile markers 5 and 14—spanning from the Perdido River Bridge east past Davis Highway. I-110 will see similar disruptions from I-10 to U.S. 98 as crews complete paving and striping. FDOT says law enforcement and traffic flaggers will be stationed in work zones to keep traffic moving safely.

Beyond the interstates, State Road 295 (Navy Boulevard) will experience outside lane closures between Barrancas and West Fairfield Drive during the same nightly window for concrete work. U.S. 90 (Scenic Highway) and U.S. 90A (West Nine Mile Road) are also slated for resurfacing, with U.S. 90A seeing daytime lane closures from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. State Road 292 (Gulf Beach Highway) near Patton Drive and Mills Avenue continues to operate at a reduced 35 mph speed limit with median devices in place.

Longer-term, drivers should note that Garden Street between Pace Boulevard and North Donelson Street remains reduced to two lanes (one per direction) through late 2026 as stormwater drainage work continues, and on-street parking is closed between A Street and L Street. FDOT recommends allowing extra travel time and staying alert for flaggers and reduced speed zones throughout the coming week.

item.title: Escambia County meetings next week: Bayou Marcus workshops, regular commission session
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Escambia County commissioners and boards have a full calendar next week, highlighted by three public workshops on the Bayou Marcus Basin Study and the county's regular commission meeting. The Bayou Marcus Basin Study workshops are open to the public and scheduled for Monday and Tuesday at 4 p.m., and Wednesday at 10 a.m., all at Lexington Terrace…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County commissioners and boards have a full calendar next week, highlighted by three public workshops on the Bayou Marcus Basin Study and the county's regular commission meeting.

The Bayou Marcus Basin Study workshops are open to the public and scheduled for Monday and Tuesday at 4 p.m., and Wednesday at 10 a.m., all at Lexington Terrace Community Center on South Old Corry Field Road. The study examines the basin's environmental and development challenges.

Other key meetings include an environmental enforcement special magistrate hearing Tuesday afternoon; development review and estuary program meetings Wednesday; and a Community Redevelopment Agency session and the Gary Sansing Public Forum Thursday evening. The Board of County Commissioners' regular meeting is Thursday, Oct. 1, at 5:30 p.m. at the Ernie Lee Magaha Government Building, 221 Palafox Place.

All agendas are available through MyEscambia.com. Commission meetings are broadcast live on channel 4 (Cox), channel 98 (Spectrum and Mediacom on Pensacola Beach), and channel 99 (AT&T U-verse). For accessibility accommodations, contact Human Resources at 850-595-3279.

item.title: USPS Sets December Holiday Shipping Deadlines for Pensacola
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The U.S. Postal Service has released its recommended mailing and shipping dates for the 2026 holiday season, and customers in the Pensacola area should mark their calendars now if they want packages to arrive by Christmas. According to USPS, mail and packages sent through the lower 48 states must meet these deadlines to guarantee delivery by…
item.content:encoded:
The U.S. Postal Service has released its recommended mailing and shipping dates for the 2026 holiday season, and customers in the Pensacola area should mark their calendars now if they want packages to arrive by Christmas.

According to USPS, mail and packages sent through the lower 48 states must meet these deadlines to guarantee delivery by December 25: Ground Advantage service by December 17, First-Class Mail by December 17, Priority Mail by December 18, and Priority Mail Express by December 19. Those shipping to Alaska, Hawaii, or U.S. territories face slightly earlier cutoffs, starting with Ground Advantage on December 16.

The postal service emphasized that holiday shoppers should mail and ship packages as early as possible, especially during the busy season when delivery times can stretch. Customers shipping to military addresses or international locations should check the USPS website starting in mid-October for additional deadline information specific to those destinations.

For packaging tips, restricted items lists, and local Post Office hours, the USPS recommends visiting usps.com or the USPS YouTube channel. More detailed holiday preparation resources are available at usps.com/holidaynews.

item.content:encoded:
Abigail Lynch, a student at Tate High School in North Escambia County, has earned recognition as a Commended Student in the 2027 National Merit Scholarship Program, placing her among the nation's highest-performing test takers.

Lynch's achievement is based on her performance on the Preliminary SAT/National Merit Scholarship Qualifying Test (PSAT/NMSQT), which she completed during her junior year. The National Merit Commended Student designation recognizes exceptional academic performance and puts her in an elite group of students nationwide.

The honor reflects the rigor of her coursework and test preparation at Tate High, one of Escambia County's public secondary schools. Lynch's recognition adds to the school's ongoing record of student achievement and college readiness.

item.content:encoded:
A drier air mass is moving into the North Escambia area through the weekend, bringing mostly sunny conditions and temperatures running slightly below normal for late September.

Friday should be sunny with highs near 84 degrees and light northeast winds at 5 to 10 mph. Friday night will see mostly clear skies with lows dropping to around 62 degrees and calm winds, according to the National Weather Service forecast.

The cooler, drier conditions should persist through the weekend, offering a pleasant change of pace from the typical late-summer humidity that often dominates the Pensacola area this time of year.

item.title: Cantonment Man Charged in Drug Raid, May Shooting Case

Antonio Krishawn Thompson, 22, is being held in the Escambia County Jail without bond. According to the Escambia County Sheriff's…
item.content:encoded:
A Cantonment resident is facing multiple felony charges following a narcotics search warrant executed at his home, and has also been charged in connection with a shooting incident originally classified as accidental.

Antonio Krishawn Thompson, 22, is being held in the Escambia County Jail without bond. According to the Escambia County Sheriff's Office, the charges stem from both the recent drug raid and his alleged involvement in a May shooting that investigators have since reclassified.

Thompson faces trafficking and firearms charges related to the search warrant execution. A woman was also arrested in connection with the investigation, though specific details about her charges were not immediately available.

The May shooting, which was initially believed to be accidental, is now being treated as a criminal matter. The Sheriff's Office has not yet released full details about the circumstances that led investigators to change the classification of that incident.

item.title: McKenzie Farms corn maze opens in Fairhope as tribute to fallen farmer
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: McKenzie Farms in Fairhope, Alabama has opened its corn maze for a second season, but this year the attraction carries deeper meaning as a tribute to a farmer who died in an accident, according to WKRG News 5. The seasonal fall tradition draws families to navigate the intricate paths cut through the cornfield, offering a popular weekend activity…
item.content:encoded:
McKenzie Farms in Fairhope, Alabama has opened its corn maze for a second season, but this year the attraction carries deeper meaning as a tribute to a farmer who died in an accident, according to WKRG News 5.

The seasonal fall tradition draws families to navigate the intricate paths cut through the cornfield, offering a popular weekend activity for the area. While the maze itself returns as an annual fixture, organizers have incorporated the remembrance into this year's experience.

The farm has become a gathering spot for the community during the fall season, combining the appeal of a classic harvest-time activity with a meaningful acknowledgment of loss. Details about the specific accident and the farmer being honored were not immediately available.
